A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VIDD research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison across the revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original computational experiments on protein design, regulatory DNA generation, and molecular docking, including reward, naturalness, diversity, and training-curve results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments across all three domains and reports additional update-interval, roll-in-mixture, and reward–diversity analyses.

M1.justification: Within the retained three-phase framework, Equations (6)–(7) explicitly add state-dependent value normalization, and Algorithm 1 estimates the additional value at x_t. Section 4.1 switches the adaptive roll-in branch from the current student to the periodically updated roll-out policy. The increasing mixture schedule is replaced by task-dependent validation selection described in Appendix E.4.

E1.justification: The standalone protein globularity task is removed from the experimental description, reward details, results, and visualizations. SS-match, PD-L1 and IFNAR2 binder design, HepG2 enhancer generation, and Parp1 molecular docking remain, using the same underlying data sources. The additional binder analyses introduce no new target population or task.

E2.justification: The main baseline sets remain unchanged, including SFT, DDPP, DDPO, Best-of-N, and DNA-specific DRAKES. However, v2 Table 7 newly compares VIDD with VIDD+BoN (N=128) on the already covered PD-L1 and IFNAR2 tasks; v1 evaluated this combined method only on other tasks.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes the reported DNA learning rate from 1e-3 to 1e-4, and Table 4 changes protein update interval K from 5 to '5/50' without explaining the allocation. New ablations vary K and the roll-in mixture. Training curves use training steps in v2 Figure 5, replacing the reward-query axis in v1 Figure 3. These reported revisions do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds DNA update-interval sensitivity (Table 8), a PD-L1 roll-in-mixture ablation (Figure 4), and checkpoint-based reward–diversity plots for three protein tasks (Figure 6). Training-curve analysis is revised and extended to binder tasks. Conversely, v1's globularity learning curve and explicit continued-training-to-collapse comparison in Table 12 are removed, substantially changing the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same median/50% quantile reporting and Table 1 description of standard errors and 95% confidence intervals. No changed repeated-run counts, experimental seed specifications, or significance-testing procedures are reported. The new scatter-plot points represent training checkpoints.

E6.justification: Table 1 materially revises results: VIDD SS-match increases from 0.69±0.13 to 0.83±0.01, while DDPO changes from 0.19±0.17 to 0.81±0.02, overtaking DDPP's retained 0.60±0.07. VIDD DNA activity changes from 7.44±0.34 to 8.28±0.18 while 3-mer correlation falls from 0.509 to 0.162. These are revised results under changed method/settings, not controlled version-to-version gains. Table 2 also revises PD-L1 Best-of-N ipTM from 0.1999 to 0.2662. New binder-combination and ablation results accompany removal of globularity and collapsed-model entries.

T1.justification: The soft-optimal policy/value definitions, Theorem 1, and the proofs and KL derivations in Appendices A–B remain unchanged. The normalizer made explicit in the revised algorithm was already present in Equation (5) and Appendix B; no new theoretical result, assumption, or derivation is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstracts, contribution statements, and conclusions retain the central claims: VIDD uses off-policy iterative distillation and forward KL optimization for potentially non-differentiable rewards, improving stability and sample efficiency across protein, DNA, and small-molecule design. The revised supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E replaces the explicit warning that continued VIDD training causes collapse and poor generative quality with an interpretation emphasizing its expanded achievable reward–diversity region. It also adds a task-dependent mixture-selection qualification. Section 1.1 softens the criticism of inference-time methods, while the proxy-reward limitations in Appendix C.2 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract adds a source-code-release statement and repository link. Hyperparameter tables are revised, and Appendix E.4 describes validation-based mixture selection. Conversely, v1's token-level diversity calculation description and explicit diversity≥0.5 reporting restriction are omitted. Hardware and software disclosures remain unchanged; omission of the restriction does not establish that actual selection changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Mnih et al. (2015) when motivating lazy updates and removes Pace and Hermans (1975) alongside the globularity task. Section 1.1 replaces the claim that inference-time methods struggle to produce large reward gains with the narrower observation that they do not improve the underlying model, emphasizing compatibility with fine-tuning.

P1.justification: The overall section organization and most prose remain intact. Local rewrites affect related work, roll-in explanations, and experimental interpretation; Appendix E gains a DNA subsection and reorganizes protein analyses. The author footnotes and abstract also receive limited edits.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially reworked: Table 1 replaces globularity columns with SS-match diversity, Figure 3 becomes a protein-structure display, and new mixture, training-curve, and reward–diversity figures appear. Appendix tables add binder-combination and K-sensitivity displays while removing the collapsed-model table. SS-match diversity partly moves from v1 Table 9 into the main table. The molecular gallery is retained as Figure 7, formerly Figure 5, despite removal of its main-text preview.

improvement.justification: The new component ablations and reward–diversity plots strengthen validation of VIDD's design choices, and the code-release link improves access information. However, v2 removes explicit collapsed-model results, the diversity computation description, and the reporting threshold. It also replaces reward-query efficiency plots with training-step plots while retaining sample-efficiency claims. These gains in diagnostic evidence coexist with losses in reproducibility and direct support for retained claims, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
